summary: The implementation of the failure simulation in the service.py file is causing a 50% failure rate instead of the intended 10% due to the use of a hardcoded 0.50 probability threshold in the random failure logic. Specifically, in the function should_fail(flag_enabled), when enabled, it returns true (failure) if random.random() < 0.50, which results in approximately 50% failures. The comment and the intended behavior indicate that the failure rate should be 10%, but the code has an erroneous 0.50 threshold instead of 0.10.
hypotheses: The failure rate is directly controlled by the threshold in random.random() comparison in should_fail().
The hardcoded 0.50 value is the root cause of the discrepancy between expected (10%) and actual (50%) failure rates.
Correcting this threshold from 0.50 to 0.10 will align the failure rate with the intended 10%.

evidence.summary: Function should_fail(flag_enabled) improperly uses 0.50 threshold causing 50% failure rate instead of intended 10%.
